correctness.rationale: For the quantified positive domain, the normalized velocity decreases and height increases. Exact left-rectangle integral comparison bounds the velocity tail by the arctangent tail with a one-step correction. Strict finite-time capture and positive-escape tests give two nonempty disjoint open outcome sets. Order preservation and the critical limit \(y_nu_n\to q\) exclude two critical initial velocities. Square-root growth at the unique threshold and ballistic escape with the \(q/v\) logarithmic height coefficient follow from the tail comparison and summable corrections. At \(q=1\), an exact polynomial identity proves the invariant separating hyperbola; the squared-height recurrence yields the \(\frac12\log n\) term. The finite exact rational identities, critical test orbits, basin certificates, and diagnostic all passed, and are explicitly not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The source motivates whether its neutral line of equilibria captures trajectories or shares phase space with escaping orbits. The new theorem identifies a unique global threshold in a natural positive-monotone parameter interval and proves three distinct asymptotic growth regimes, including the critical square-root law, an exact algebraic separator at the natural endpoint, and a logarithmic correction to ballistic escape. Strict finite-time outcome certificates make the global classification reproducibly usable beyond local linearization or finite simulations.
